messages:
maya.dev: quick report. found flaky bundler behavior with conditional exports + subpath exports. repro attached and minimal steps below.

kevin: which bundler versions/node? paste package.json snippet please.

maya.dev: package.json snippet:
```json
{
  "name": "mini-lib",
  "version": "0.0.1",
  "exports": {
    ".": {
      "import": "./dist/esm/index.js",
      "require": "./dist/cjs/index.js"
    },
    "./widget": {
      "import": "./dist/esm/widget.js",
      "require": "./dist/cjs/widget.js"
    }
  },
  "types": "dist/types/index.d.ts"
}
```
Tested: Node 18/20, Rollup 3.8, Webpack 5.80, Vite 4.1.0.

Observed:
- Rollup + default node-resolve sometimes resolves consumer require() to the esm file -> runtime "Unexpected token 'export'".
- Webpack dev server fine, but production bundle (mode=production) fails when importing subpath ./widget -> resolves to esm and Terser mangles error timing so only prod fails.
- Vite SSR build targeting Cloudflare Workers -> "ReferenceError: exports is not defined" when lib ended up mixed cjs/esm.

sasha: I can reproduce on Node 20 + rollup. quick workaround: set node-resolve exportConditions to include 'require' and 'node' and preferBuiltins:false. plugin version matters.

oliver: can you share the tiny repro so we can try CI?

maya.dev: gist with repo layout: https://gist.github.com/fake/mini-repro (tarball in link). steps: clone, yarn, yarn build:lib (tsc -> dist/esm & dist/cjs), cd consumer-rollup, yarn, yarn build, node consumer-rollup/dist/index.js -> see Unexpected token export for require path.

kevin: confirmed. with rollup v3.8 + @rollup/plugin-node-resolve v14 you need resolve({ exportConditions: ['node','require','default'] }) to prefer cjs. otherwise it prefers import.

maya.dev: also hit TS typing issues: when bundler picks esm entry but types point to dist/types, consumer TS sometimes loses types for subpath imports (./widget) unless moduleResolution=node16 or bundler mode set.

oliver: edge-specific note: Vite SSR + Workers want clean ESM output. if your package has cjs in exports and bundler hits commonjs transform, the worker runtime rejects. adding a "browser" field pointing to esm build helped one user.

kevin: webpack tip: ensure resolve.mainFields includes ['exports','module','main'] so exports wins. sometimes swapping order changes which file is bundled.

maya.dev: build-bot: CI failed after adding subpath exports -> job 5012 failed with Unexpected token export in consumer-rollup node 18 test.

build-bot: CI logs snippet:
[error] consumer-rollup/dist/index.js:1
  \u001b[31mThrown:\u001b[39m Unexpected token 'export'

sasha: suggested long-term fixes: publish dual entrypoints (esm + cjs) with explicit exports mapping for subpaths, add module & browser fields, and document consumer bundler configs in SDK migration guide. also add small repro and matrix tests in repo.

kevin: short patch I pushed in repo fork: add an explicit 'node' condition in exports pointing to cjs for Node consumers. PR referenced in gist.

maya.dev: filing devex issue to track docs + CI test matrix (rollup/webpack/vite). will add repro and config snippets. thanks. :thumbsup:

oliver: can we add CI job to run consumer builds across the three bundlers so this doesn't regress?

maya.dev: yes. plan to add matrix next sprint.

sasha: I'll write a short doc with recommended package.json layouts, rollup/webpack/vite resolver configs, and TS moduleResolution notes. will ping SDK team for review.

maya.dev: thanks everyone. drop other cases here if you see different permutations. :pray:
